name: Stacy v. Thermo-Dynamics Corp. (Video Privacy Protection Act legislative history)
summary: Congress enacted the VPPA in 1988 to prohibit video providers from disclosing customers' rental or viewing records without consent, creating a private right of action with statutory damages of at least $2,500 per violation.
significance: The VPPA itself and its legislative history — triggered by publication of Judge Bork's video rental records — are cited by Salazar to show that Congress specifically identified video-viewing data as a protected privacy interest warranting a private right of action.
